name: LiveUIBench
scope: dev and public_test only; sealed_test excluded

cases.scenario: Weekly commute soundtrack

context.lastWeekMemory: remembering what I picked last week so I can tweak it instead of starting over

intentions.intention: I want an app where each week I set the vibe for my drive to work and it builds a fresh commute playlist, remembering what I picked last week so I can tweak it instead of starting over.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows an empty commute-playlist shell. I type the vibe 'upbeat indie' and seed artists Noah Bennett and Ethan Wallace, submit, and ~20 matched indie songs appear in a newly created commute playlist (the app names the playlist itself; any clear commute/vibe-derived name is fine). I tweak this week's vibe to 'mellow indie' and the visible track list re-renders around the new vibe instead of starting a new playlist. Reopening later it still shows that same commute playlist with my 'mellow indie' vibe remembered, ready for me to tweak again next week.

episodes.userMessage: Vibe is upbeat indie, seed artists Phoenix and Two Door Cinema Club, about 20 songs for Monday Commute.
Tweak this week's vibe to mellow indie.

cases.scenario: Adaptive workout playlist

intentions.intention: I want a personal app where I pick a seed genre and a peak artist, and it assembles my workout playlist by intensity zones from that pick, letting me bump the energy up or down between sessions and keeping my chosen tracks saved so each gym day I just adjust rather than rebuild.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Opening shows three empty zone slots. I pick genre 'EDM' and peak artist Jasper Skye, submit, and each zone fills with matched songs and a workout playlist is created and shown (the app names the playlist itself; any clear workout-derived name is fine). I raise the peak zone intensity and only the peak slot re-renders with harder tracks while warmup and cooldown stay unchanged. Reopening later that same playlist still shows my three zones intact, and I add the peak tracks to my play queue for the session.

episodes.userMessage: Use genre EDM and peak artist Jasper Skye to assemble my workout playlist by intensity zones.
Raise the peak zone intensity.

cases.scenario: One new genre each week

intentions.intention: I want an app that helps me explore one unfamiliar genre per week: it shows me the genres available in the music catalog, I pick one to be this week's genre, it surfaces a starter set of songs, I mark which songs I actually liked, and it remembers my ratings so over time it steers toward the corners of the genre I enjoy.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app lists the genres available in the real catalog and I choose 'reggae' as this week's genre, asking for a 15-song starter set; submitting shows 15 reggae songs drawn from the catalog. I play three of them first — only a song I have actually heard can be kept — then like those three; they are marked liked in my real library and move into a 'kept' section that reads '3 kept'. Reopening later, the app still shows reggae as the current genre with my three kept songs remembered.

episodes.userMessage: Show me the genres available in the music catalog, choose reggae as this week's genre, and give me 15 reggae songs to start.
Play three of the reggae songs so they count as heard.
Now like those three heard songs and keep them in a '3 kept' section.

cases.scenario: Liked songs cleanup

intentions.intention: My liked songs have become a mess and I want an app that walks me through them in batches so I can sort them into themed playlists, remembering where I left off so I can chip away at it over several evenings.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app reads my liked songs (the account has 40) and offers a triage batch of 25, showing a progress marker like '25 of 40'. I assign several visible songs into the Focus and Chill playlists; each assignment moves the song into the real playlist and the playlist counts rise accordingly. Skipped songs stay liked. Reopening later shows the remaining backlog (15 left) and the playlists keep the songs previously assigned.

episodes.userMessage: Show my liked songs 25 at a time (25 of 40) so I can sort them into the Focus and Chill playlists.
Assign several visible songs into the Focus and Chill playlists, and keep skipped songs liked.

cases.scenario: Dinner party queue manager

intentions.intention: I host small dinners and want an app that builds an evening queue in courses, letting me reorder or add requests on the fly during the night while keeping the running order visible so I always know what plays next.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open I set 'warm jazz' across three courses and submit; a course-by-course queue appears with concrete songs and a 'now playing / up next' order. Mid-evening a guest asks for something classical, the app searches and inserts classical matches into the dessert course, and the up-next list updates to show them alongside the jazz tracks. I then reorder the queue on the fly — moving one of those classical tracks ahead of the remaining jazz — and the visible running order changes to match. Reopening after a break, the queue persists showing what already played, my reordering, and what is still to come.

episodes.userMessage: Set warm jazz across three courses.
Add something classical into the dessert course.
Move that classical track ahead of the remaining jazz so it shows up next in the queue.

cases.scenario: Kids bedtime wind-down

context.windDownRule: volume and track softness ease down in proportion to time remaining; changing the length rescales the whole curve rather than cutting the last songs

intentions.intention: I want a nightly wind-down app for my kids that plays progressively calmer songs, easing the volume and the softness down in proportion to how much time is left, and lets me adjust how long and how mellow it goes — when I change the length it should rescale the whole calm curve, not just chop off the last songs — saving our routine so each night I just press start and tweak if needed.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows an empty 'Lights Out' routine; I set mood 'gentle acoustic' and 30 minutes, submit, and a descending-calm song list appears and starts playing. I make it calmer by having it drop the player volume to 4 and re-render the list with proportionally softer tracks as bedtime approaches, and the arc gets gentler across its whole length while playback continues. Reopening the next night 'Lights Out' is remembered exactly, and I shorten it to 20 minutes — the app rescales the descending-calm arc proportionally across the shorter window instead of just trimming the tail tracks — before I press play.

episodes.userMessage: Mood gentle acoustic, 30 minutes, build the Lights Out routine and start playing.
Make it calmer: drop the player volume to 4 and re-render the list with proportionally softer tracks as bedtime approaches.
Shorten tonight to 20 minutes, but rescale the wind-down proportionally — don't just chop the last songs.

cases.scenario: Study focus sessions

intentions.intention: I want an app that runs my study sessions with focus music and logs which sessions actually helped, remembering my best soundtracks so it can lean on them when I need to concentrate again.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On first open there are no proven sets yet, so the app asks what to focus with; I pick genre 'classical' and a 90-minute goal, and it starts a focus playlist named 'Organic Chemistry Focus' and shows a session card. I rate the session 'helped', it saves, and the playlist is tagged a keeper, moving into a 'proven focus sets' list. From the next block on the app leads with proven sets instead of asking me to pick a genre again: I start one straight from that list, and rating it 'distracting' drops it from the proven list, with the change persisting on reopen.

episodes.userMessage: Start a 90-minute classical focus session and make Organic Chemistry Focus the playlist.
Rate Organic Chemistry Focus as helped so it becomes a proven focus set.
Start my next block straight from proven focus sets, then rate it distracting.

cases.scenario: Artist catalog deep-dive

intentions.intention: When I discover an artist I love I want an app that walks me through their whole catalog album by album, tracking which I've heard and liked so I can return and pick up the deep-dive where I stopped.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open I enter 'Aria Sterling' and the app lists her albums with a 'Velvet Underground' starting point and an untouched progress bar. I open Velvet Underground and like a few tracks; liking them is what marks the album heard, so the progress bar advances to '1 of 3' on its own without me tagging it. Reopening later the app remembers Aria Sterling and shows Velvet Underground as done, so I continue to the next album, and that new progress persists on the next reopen.

episodes.userMessage: Show me Aria Sterling's albums and start my deep dive with Velvet Underground.
Open Velvet Underground and like a few tracks - that should count the album as heard and move my deep dive to 1 of 3.

cases.scenario: Running cadence playlist

context.model: one playlist per cadence; raising the cadence creates a new playlist and preserves the previous one

intentions.intention: I want a running app that builds a cadence-matched playlist for my target step rate, and when my pace improves it saves a new playlist for the new cadence while keeping the previous cadence's playlist intact — so I end up with a small library of tempo playlists, one per cadence, to pick from before each run.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows no tempo playlists yet; I set cadence 170 and genre 'rock', submit, and a matched song list appears with a playlist 'Tempo Run 170' created. When my pace improves I bump the target to 175 cadence — the app creates a NEW playlist 'Tempo Run 175' with tracks matched to the faster tempo and keeps 'Tempo Run 170' untouched as the playlist for my old cadence. Reopening before my next run, both 'Tempo Run 170' and 'Tempo Run 175' are still there, and I queue the 175 one to start immediately.

episodes.userMessage: Set up Tempo Run 170 at 170 cadence with rock songs.
My pace improved — bump to 175 cadence, but save it as a new playlist Tempo Run 175 and keep Tempo Run 170 as it is.

cases.scenario: Monthly mood-in-songs journal

intentions.intention: I want an app where I log my mood each day by picking a song that captures it, building a monthly musical diary I can reopen to see how the month felt and turn into a playlist at the end.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the July diary is empty; I describe today's mood 'restless', the app suggests real songs (fetched from spotify) and I pick one, which appears as a dated diary entry for the day I choose. I log a second entry under another date I choose and the diary grows to two dated song entries, both visible together. Reopening later my earlier entries persist in date order as distinct dated entries (not merged into a summary), and I hit 'make playlist', creating a real spotify playlist containing my logged songs (the app may choose the playlist name).

episodes.userMessage: Today's mood is restless; suggest songs seeded by Ethan Wallace and log the one I pick.
At month's end, make a July diary playlist from all my logged songs.

cases.scenario: Road trip playlist by leg

intentions.intention: We're driving cross-country and I want an app that builds our road-trip playlist leg by leg, letting each of us add picks and adjust the vibe per stretch, keeping the whole trip's music saved so we can extend it as the route grows.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open I name the trip 'PCH Drive' and set three legs with a 'rock' base; submitting fills each leg with songs and creates a trip playlist. A rider requests Zoey James — I add her to the coast-morning leg — and I shift the desert-sunset leg's vibe to 'country', so those two legs re-render while the third stays put. Reopening later, 'PCH Drive' persists with all three legs, and I add a new 'mountain pass' leg that appends fresh songs without disturbing the earlier legs.

episodes.userMessage: Name the trip PCH Drive, set three legs with a rock base, fill each leg with songs, and create the trip playlist.
A rider requests Zoey James, so add her to the coast-morning leg, and shift the desert-sunset leg's vibe to country; keep the third leg the same.
Add a new mountain pass leg that appends fresh songs without disturbing the earlier legs.

cases.scenario: Language immersion rotation

context.studyMethod: daily Portuguese listening-comprehension practice: loop each song in the active rotation until its lyrics can be followed by ear without help, then retire it to the mastered list

intentions.intention: I'm studying Portuguese and songs are my daily listening-comprehension practice: I loop each song until I can follow the lyrics by ear, because hearing vocabulary set to music makes it stick. I want an app that keeps a rotating practice pool of songs seeded from artists I pick, lets me retire a song to a mastered list once I can understand it without help, and lets me seed new artists so my active rotation always has fresh listening material and everything is remembered between sessions.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows an empty 'PT Practice' pool for my Portuguese listening practice; I add seed artist Isabella Cruz and her songs appear and are saved to the playlist as my active rotation of listening material. I mark two songs 'mastered' — meaning I can now follow their lyrics by ear without help — and they move out of the active rotation into a mastered list, dropping the active count so the rotation only holds songs I'm still learning. Reopening later, 'PT Practice' persists with the mastered songs still set aside from the active rotation, and the app offers a way to seed another artist (e.g. Seraphina Dawn) to refill it with fresh listening material.

episodes.userMessage: Add Isabella Cruz to my PT Practice pool.
Mark two songs as mastered and move them out of the active rotation into the mastered list.

cases.scenario: Wish list price-drop watch

priceCheck.trigger: user asks for a fresh price check on open or on demand
priceCheck.behavior: pull each watched product's current price live from the Amazon catalog and compare it against the saved target

intentions.intention: I keep a wish list of things I want but won't pay full price for. I want an app that acts as my price monitor: I set a target price for each saved item, and whenever I open it or ask it to check, it pulls the live Amazon price of every watched item and compares it against my target, so I can see which ones have finally dropped to or below my number and move those into my cart.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On first open I add my three watched items; the app finds them in the catalog and saves them to my real wish list beside my target prices, pulling each one's live Amazon price and comparing it to my target: Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling headphones at $350.00 vs my $249 target, Instant Pot Duo 6-Quart Pressure Cooker at $89.00 vs $79, and Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (10th Generation) at $130.00 vs $110 — each with a red 'still above' badge. I submit a new target of $260 for the headphones; the row recomputes the price-vs-target comparison, the gap-to-target shrinks to $90, and the badge stays red. I then raise the Instant Pot target to $90; since its live price is $89.00 the comparison flips the badge to green 'ready' and a 'Move to cart' button appears, which I tap to move it into my real cart. Reopening later, the app re-pulls current prices, still remembers every target I set, keeps the Instant Pot marked as moved to cart, and the headphones and Kindle remain red because their re-pulled prices are unchanged. Finally I ask it to run a fresh price check: the app pulls each watched product's current price live from the Amazon catalog — $350.00 for the headphones, $89.00 for the Instant Pot, $130.00 for the Kindle — and compares each against my targets of $260, $90, and $110, showing the headphones and Kindle still above while the Instant Pot stays at or below target and keeps its moved-to-cart mark.

episodes.userMessage: Add Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling headphones, Instant Pot Duo 6-Quart Pressure Cooker, and Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (10th Generation) to my watch list from my wish list, with targets of $249, $79, and $110.
Change the Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling headphones target to $260, then raise the Instant Pot Duo 6-Quart Pressure Cooker target to $90 and move it to cart.
Run a fresh price check now: pull the current Amazon prices for all three watched items and compare each against my target — show which are still above and which are ready.

cases.scenario: Household consumables restock

staples: Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent
Dawn Ultra Dishwashing Liquid Dish Soap, Original Scent

intentions.intention: Make me a restock pad for the household basics I buy over and over. I'll type in my staples; it should match each one to its real Amazon catalog product, let me mark what's running low, and each time I come back I bulk-add the low items to my Amazon cart with the right quantities so the cart is staged and ready to check out.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The pad opens empty with a place to enter staples; I type my three staples — 'Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent', 'Dawn Ultra Dishwashing Liquid Dish Soap, Original Scent', and 'Glad Large Trash Bags' — and each is matched to its real catalog product with a price and a running-low toggle. I flip the detergent and the trash bags to low and bulk-add them; the real Amazon cart now holds those 2 items and the pad shows a cart preview with the subtotal read back from the cart. I bump the trash bags quantity from 1 to 2 and the real cart quantity and subtotal update. Reopening the pad later, all three staples are still listed with the dish soap not-low, and the real cart still holds the detergent plus the trash bags at quantity 2.

episodes.userMessage: Add these staples to my restock pad: Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent, Dawn Ultra Dishwashing Liquid Dish Soap, Original Scent, and Glad Large Trash Bags. Mark the detergent and trash bags as running low and bulk-add the low items to my Amazon cart.

assertions.value: Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent

episodes.userMessage: Update the Glad Large Trash Bags quantity in my cart from 1 to 2.

cases.scenario: Per-recipient gift planning

intentions.intention: Every gifting season I lose track of who I'm buying for. I want a planner where I list each person with a budget, stage candidate gifts under their name into my Amazon cart so they're ready to buy, and reopen it later to see who still needs something and whose gift is already staged in the cart.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The planner opens with three recipient cards (Mom $80 birthday, Leo $50 graduation, Priya $25 housewarming), each with an empty gift slot. I search for a gift for Mom and stage the IKEA Riggad LED Work Lamp with Wireless Charging at $70.00 under her card, which the app also saves to my real wish list; her card shows $70 of $80 used with a green 'within budget' bar. I revise by adding a Pottery Barn Flameless Wax Pillar Candle at $19.50 for Mom, pushing her to $89.50; the bar turns amber 'over budget' and warns me. I remove the candle to get back to $70, then stage an Anker PowerCore 10000 Portable Charger at $30.00 under Leo and bulk-add it to my Amazon cart so it's staged and ready to buy, moving his card to a 'Ready to buy' column. Reopening the planner next week, Mom is still staged-but-not-bought at $70 of $80, Leo stays in Ready to buy with his charger still in the cart, Priya still shows an empty slot, and all three budgets persist exactly as I set them.

episodes.userMessage: Search for a gift for Mom and stage the IKEA Riggad LED Work Lamp with Wireless Charging under her card.

assertions.value: IKEA Riggad LED Work Lamp with Wireless Charging

episodes.userMessage: Add the Pottery Barn Flameless Wax Pillar Candle for Mom, then remove it and stage the Anker PowerCore 10000 Portable Charger for Leo by adding it to my Amazon cart so it's ready to buy.

assertions.value: IKEA Riggad LED Work Lamp with Wireless Charging

cases.scenario: Returns and refund status board

intentions.intention: I return things fairly often and never know which refunds have actually landed. Build me a board where I log each return I've started — the item, my reason, and its current status — letting me pick the return carrier from Amazon's real deliverer list and attach a matching catalog product to each card, update a status when a refund lands, and find everything intact when I reopen it.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The board opens with an empty 'In progress' column and a form to log a return. I log a return for my 'Adidas Ultraboost 21' running shoes (size 10) with reason 'wrong size' and status 'awaiting pickup', picking a carrier from Amazon's real return-deliverer list (UPS, USPS, and FedEx) and attaching the matching 'Adidas Ultraboost 21 Men's Shoe' looked up in the real catalog; the card appears with its reason, carrier, and status. I add a second return for my 'TaoTronics LED Desk Lamp' with reason 'defective', attaching its matching catalog product the same way, and the board shows two pending cards with a count of 2. I then update the Ultraboost card to 'refund issued' with a note that I'll reorder in size 11, while the lamp stays 'awaiting pickup'. Reopening the board later, both cards persist exactly as I recorded them — the shoes at 'refund issued' with the size-11 note and the lamp still pending.

episodes.userMessage: Log a return for my Adidas Ultraboost 21 running shoes, size 10, with reason wrong size, status awaiting pickup, use UPS from the return deliverer list, and attach the matching Ultraboost shoe product from the catalog.

Add a second return for my TaoTronics LED Desk Lamp with reason defective and attach its matching catalog product, and update the Ultraboost card to refund issued with a note that I'll reorder in size 11.

cases.scenario: Delivered-orders review backlog

recentPurchases: OXO Good Grips Bamboo Cutting Board
Belkin Boost Charge USB-C + USB-A Wall Charger

toReview: OXO Good Grips Bamboo Cutting Board
Belkin Boost Charge USB-C + USB-A Wall Charger

intentions.intention: I mean to review the stuff I buy but never get around to it. I want a backlog where I list the recent purchases I still owe a review, draft and post star ratings for them, and have it remember which ones I've already covered when I come back.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open I enter the three items I bought recently — an OXO Good Grips Bamboo Cutting Board, a Belkin Boost Charge USB-C + USB-A Wall Charger, and a Manduka PRO Yoga Mat — and the app matches each to its catalog product and shows a 'To review' badge on all three. I write a 5-star review for the cutting board with a short note; it posts to the real product and the item flips to a 'Reviewed' section showing my star count. I then post a 2-star review for the charger since it stopped working after a month, so the To-review count drops to 1 (just the yoga mat). Later I decide the charger deserves 3 stars and edit my existing review; the displayed rating updates from 2 to 3. Reopening the backlog, the cutting board and charger remain in Reviewed with my latest ratings re-pulled from each product's review list, the yoga mat still shows To review, and my edited 3-star text persists.

episodes.userMessage: Create my review backlog from these recent purchases: OXO Good Grips Bamboo Cutting Board, Belkin Boost Charge USB-C + USB-A Wall Charger, and Manduka PRO Yoga Mat. Then post a 5-star review with a short note for the cutting board and a 2-star review for the charger since it stopped working after a month. Badge each item 'To review' until I post its review, then flip it to 'Reviewed'.

assertions.value: OXO Good Grips Bamboo Cutting Board
Belkin Boost Charge USB-C + USB-A Wall Charger

episodes.userMessage: Edit my existing review for the Belkin Boost Charge USB-C + USB-A Wall Charger from 2 stars to 3 stars.

assertions.value: Belkin Boost Charge USB-C + USB-A Wall Charger
Belkin Boost Charge USB-C + USB-A Wall Charger
OXO Good Grips Bamboo Cutting Board

cases.scenario: Prime membership value ledger

context.order_history: still empty (fresh account — logged entries are manual estimates, not order-derived)

intentions.intention: I can never tell whether Prime would actually pay for itself. Give me a ledger that pulls the real plan prices, lets me log each month what I would have saved on fast shipping and deals sanity-checked against my order history, and tells me if I'm ahead of the yearly cost, then reopen it to keep tallying toward my subscribe-or-not decision.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the ledger is an empty shell — no months logged yet, just an input for my request. When I submit my request naming the yearly plan as the break-even target and my two months, the ledger pulls the real Prime plans via the plans API (monthly $15, yearly $140), checks my subscriptions (none yet), sets the $140 yearly plan as my break-even target, and logs the two months I supplied — May $22 and June $18.50 — totaling $40.50 with a status line 'still $99.50 to break even'. I add a July saving of $31 in fast-shipping value; the ledger checks my order history (still empty — it notes the entry is a manual estimate, not order-derived) and the running total climbs to $71.50 with the gap narrowing to $68.50. I then correct June's entry from $18.50 up to $28; the total recomputes to $81 and the gap to $59. Reopening the ledger later, it still shows the $140 yearly target re-pulled fresh from the plans API, keeps all three months with the corrected June figure and the cumulative $81, and flags whether subscribing looks worth it based on the trend.

episodes.userMessage: Give me a ledger for whether Prime would pay for itself using the yearly plan as the break-even target and my logged months May $22 and June $18.50.
Add a July saving of $31 in fast-shipping value, then correct June's entry from $18.50 up to $28.

cases.scenario: Capped monthly shopping cart

intentions.intention: I overspend when I shop online, so I want a helper where I set a monthly spending cap, build my cart up against it, and get warned before I blow past the limit; when the month is done I archive it and start the next one with a fresh cap.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The helper opens with my $150 July cap and an empty cart meter at $0. I add a CamelBak Eddy+ Water Bottle at $20.00 and an OtterBox Symmetry phone case at $40.00 to my real cart; the meter fills to $60 of $150 in the green zone. I keep going with two puzzle books at $13.00 and $8.00, bringing it to $81, and then add a Columbia Women's Heavenly Long Hooded Jacket at $170.00 that tips me to $251 — over the cap; the meter turns red and the helper warns me with an 'over cap' flag. Reopening the helper later, the cart still holds everything with the red $251-of-$150 meter and my $150 cap remembered as the default; when I then remove the jacket the meter recomputes to $81, back in the green.

episodes.userMessage: Set my July spending cap to $150 and add a CamelBak Eddy+ Water Bottle and an OtterBox Symmetry phone case to my cart.
Also add the two puzzle books and the Columbia Women's Heavenly Long Hooded Jacket, and warn me with an 'over cap' flag if that puts me over the cap.

assertions.value: Columbia Women's Heavenly Long Hooded Jacket
Columbia Women's Heavenly Long Hooded Jacket

cases.scenario: Curated trusted-seller shortlist

intentions.intention: For my photography hobby I only want to buy from sellers I trust. Build me a shortlist tool where I add sellers, keep only the highly rated ones, and reopen it to re-check their ratings before I buy gear.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The tool opens and lets me search sellers by name. I add Sony, whose live rating 4.1 clears my 4.0 threshold, landing it in my 'Trusted' list. I then add Canon at rating 4.0 (right at the threshold, Trusted) and B&H Photo Video, which falls to the 'Watch' list at 3.9. I raise my threshold to 4.1, which demotes Canon to Watch while Sony stays Trusted, and I pin Sony as my go-to. I browse products filtered to Sony's catalog to confirm quality, seeing camera gear like the Sony Alpha a6400 Mirrorless Camera at $998.00. Reopening the tool later, it re-pulls each seller's rating fresh from the API, keeps Sony pinned as trusted, still remembers my 4.1 threshold, and re-sorts the lists from the re-pulled ratings — unchanged, so Sony stays on top.

episodes.userMessage: Create a shortlist tool for sellers I trust with a 4.0 threshold, add Sony, Canon, and B&H Photo Video, and pin Sony as my go-to.
Raise my threshold to 4.1 and browse Sony products to confirm quality.

cases.scenario: Pre-purchase question follow-ups

products_considering: Le Creuset Classic Whistling Tea Kettle
context.initial_tracker_state: The tracker opens showing the two products I'm considering — the IKEA MICKE Desk and the Le Creuset Classic Whistling Tea Kettle — each with an 'Ask' box.
preexisting_answered_community_questions: Does it have a heat-resistant handle?

intentions.intention: Before I buy something I usually post a question and then forget to check for the answer. I want a tracker where I log the questions I've asked on products I'm considering and reopen it to see which got answered so I can decide to buy.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The tracker opens showing the two products I'm considering — the IKEA MICKE Desk and the Le Creuset Classic Whistling Tea Kettle — each with an 'Ask' box. I post my desk question 'Does the frame fit a 60-inch top?'; it is written to the real IKEA MICKE Desk product and appears under it marked 'awaiting answer'. I post the kettle question 'Is the interior stainless or plastic?' too, so the tracker shows two open questions and an unanswered count of 2. When I reopen the tracker later it re-pulls each product's Q&A from the store: both of my questions persist with their exact wording and remain 'awaiting answer' (no new answers exist), while the tracker distinguishes them from each product's pre-existing answered community questions shown alongside — e.g. the kettle's 'Does it have a heat-resistant handle?' and the desk's 'Does it require assembly?', each expandable to its answers — and every product row keeps an 'Add to cart' action so I can buy once satisfied. When I then ask the tracker to check both of my questions for new answers, it re-queries each question's answer list from the store: both lists come back empty so my two questions stay marked 'awaiting answer', while each product's answered community question — the desk's 'Does it require assembly?' and the kettle's 'Does it have a heat-resistant handle?' — is shown with its fetched answers, so I can see at a glance that nothing of mine has been answered yet.

episodes.userMessage: Ask on the IKEA MICKE Desk: Does the frame fit a 60-inch top?

assertions.value: Does the frame fit a 60-inch top?

episodes.userMessage: Also ask on the Le Creuset Classic Whistling Tea Kettle: Is the interior stainless or plastic?

assertions.value: Is the interior stainless or plastic?
Le Creuset Classic Whistling Tea Kettle
Does the frame fit a 60-inch top?
Is the interior stainless or plastic?

episodes.userMessage: Check both of my questions for new answers — keep any that still have none marked 'awaiting answer' — and show each product's already-answered community question with its answers.

assertions.value: Does it have a heat-resistant handle?

cases.scenario: Multi-address shipping router

intentions.intention: I ship to a few different places but my Amazon address book starts empty. Build me an address book where I enter the places I ship to as real Amazon address records; since Amazon has no default-address field, the current default is marked with a '(default)' tag kept inside that address record's name. intentions.expectedBehavior: On open I search 'laundry detergent' and real catalog results render from search_products, the Persil ProClean Liquid Laundry Detergent alongside the Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent, each with its live price. I pick the Persil plus the Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Soap and add_product_to_cart stages both, a cart panel totalling the picks. I then swap the Persil out for the cheaper Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent and the cart re-renders reflecting the swap. Reopening, show_cart still holds the staged Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent and Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Soap exactly as I left them.

intentions.intention: Every month after I stage the household restock in my Amazon cart I chase the housemates for their share by hand; I want an app that reads whatever sits in my cart, books the cart's merchandise total into our 'Maple House' splitwise group with Isla Verhoeven and Ruben Calloway, and splits it evenly three ways.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app calls show_cart and lists the staged Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent and Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Soap with the cart's merchandise total, contents that exist only because the restock app staged them in the shared world. I confirm and the app creates the 'Maple House' splitwise group with Isla Verhoeven and Ruben Calloway and record_expense books the cart total split evenly three ways, the board showing each housemate owing a third of the cart. Reopening, show_group_expenses renders the booked restock expense with each housemate's share intact and the board still names Isla Verhoeven and Ruben Calloway.

episodes.userMessage: Search Amazon for laundry detergent so I can compare the Persil ProClean Liquid Laundry Detergent against the Tide Coldwater Clean Liquid Laundry Detergent with prices, then add the Persil ProClean Liquid Laundry Detergent and the Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Soap to my cart to stage this month's restock.

cases.scenario: App1 is a pocket IOU pad that writes each small cash loan as a note card in the shared world; App2 is a payday collector that must read those exact IOU cards from the notes and fire venmo requests for the amounts on them.

intentions.intention: Friends borrow small cash off me constantly and I forget; I want a pocket IOU pad where each loan becomes a note card with who owes me, how much, and what it was for.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the IOU pad is empty. I jot the card 'IOU: Dario Fontaine owes $24' for the farmers market haul and create_note writes it, the card rendering with the amount and reason. I jot a second card 'IOU: Noor Ferrand owes $18' for the concert rideshare and it appears alongside the first. Reopening, both cards come back from search_notes with 'IOU: Dario Fontaine owes $24' and 'IOU: Noor Ferrand owes $18' intact.

intentions.intention: When payday comes I want an app that reads the IOU cards in my notes, fires a Venmo request at each person for the exact amount on their card, and tracks which requests are still unpaid.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app searches my notes for IOU cards, reads each via show_note, and lists Dario Fontaine at $24 and Noor Ferrand at $18, entries that exist only because the IOU pad wrote them into the shared world. I hit 'collect all' and create_payment_request fires a $24 Venmo request to Dario Fontaine and an $18 Venmo request to Noor Ferrand, both rows flipping to 'requested'. Reopening, show_sent_payment_requests backs both rows still pending (approved_at empty), Dario Fontaine at $24 and Noor Ferrand at $18. Dario drags his feet, so I tap nudge on his row and remind_payment_request sends a payment-request reminder from the same board.

episodes.userMessage: Jot an IOU card: IOU: Dario Fontaine owes $24, for the farmers market haul.
Add a second card: IOU: Noor Ferrand owes $18, for the concert rideshare.
Collect all: read the IOU cards in my notes and fire a Venmo request at Dario Fontaine for $24 and Noor Ferrand for $18, the exact amounts on their cards.
Dario Fontaine still hasn't paid — tap nudge on his request to remind him.

cases.scenario: Three weekly newsletters distilled into one digest note

newsletters.takeawayLine: Serif logos are back because screens finally got sharp enough to render them.

intentions.intention: Three newsletters are the only ones I read cover to cover: Marisol Vega's design letter Grid & Gradient, Tomas Lindqvist's trail letter Peak Week, and Priya Raman's cooking letter Simmer. Build me a digest app that finds this week's issue of each newsletter in my inbox and distills all three into ONE weekly note in my notes app, a section per newsletter carrying the author's takeaway sentence word for word. When I disagree with an author I want to swap in my own takeaway instead, and once a week's issues are distilled the app should archive them out of my inbox — the note is the record. Last week's digest note stays untouched next to the new one.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the three issues it found in my inbox — 'Grid & Gradient #112 — The quiet return of serif logos' from Marisol Vega (letters@gridandgradient.studio), 'Peak Week — Larch madness comes early' from Tomas Lindqvist (trail@peakweek.club), and 'Simmer #86 — Brown butter is a flavor, not a step' from Priya Raman (stove@simmerletter.kitchen) — alongside last week's existing note 'Weekly Digest — Week of Jul 13', with no note yet for this week. When I say build the digest, the app creates one note titled 'Weekly Digest — Week of Jul 20' with a section per newsletter (3 issues = 3 sections, one takeaway line each) copying each author's takeaway sentence verbatim from the email bodies: 'Serif logos are back because screens finally got sharp enough to render them.', 'Larch needles are turning two weeks early, so book your October hikes for late September.', and 'Browning the butter first turns an ordinary cookie recipe into a bakery one.'. Reopening later, 'Weekly Digest — Week of Jul 20' still holds the serif-logos line verbatim, the Simmer section still reads my replacement line, and last week's digest sits beside it untouched.

episodes.userMessage: It's Sunday — build this week's digest. Create one note titled 'Weekly Digest — Week of Jul 20' with a section per newsletter, and copy each author's 'The one-line takeaway:' sentence into its section word for word.

I want one app that keeps these day pairings together — when I set up a day it creates the alarm on my phone and builds the named playlist in my spotify, and I can add another day's pairing later when I decide, say, that Wednesdays deserve reggae.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows an empty wake-up pairing board with a way to enter a day, an alarm time, a genre, a playlist name, and the songs I want. When I set up Monday — alarm at 6:20 AM, jazz, playlist 'Monday Jazz Sunrise' with 'Whispers of Destiny', 'Moonlit Sighs', and 'Mystic Rhythms' — the app creates the 6:20 AM phone alarm, searches each named song in the spotify catalog to get its track, creates the 'Monday Jazz Sunrise' playlist and adds all three, and the Monday card shows the alarm time alongside the three titles. When I then give Wednesday to reggae — alarm at 6:50 AM, playlist 'Wednesday Reggae Lift' with 'Midnight Train', 'Serenity in the Rain', and 'Stardust Serenade' — a second phone alarm is created and the reggae playlist is built the same way, so the board now shows both day pairings. Reopening later, both pairings survive: 'Monday Jazz Sunrise' still holds 'Whispers of Destiny', 'Moonlit Sighs', and 'Mystic Rhythms', and the 6:50 AM Wednesday alarm still pairs with 'Wednesday Reggae Lift' ending in 'Stardust Serenade'.

episodes.userMessage: Set up Monday: alarm at 6:20 AM and a jazz wake-up playlist named Monday Jazz Sunrise with Whispers of Destiny, Moonlit Sighs, and Mystic Rhythms.
Wednesdays deserve reggae: alarm at 6:50 AM, playlist named Wednesday Reggae Lift with Midnight Train, Serenity in the Rain, and Stardust Serenade.

cases.scenario: Roommate security-deposit escrow: collect shares, then split the landlord refund

context.split: equal three-way between me and the two roommates
context.refundFunding: the landlord's refund check lands in my bank, so my Visa on file pulls it onto my Venmo balance before I pay the shares out

intentions.intention: When we signed the lease at 44 Corliss Ave I fronted the whole $2,400 security deposit for the three of us, and I refuse to let that money dissolve into roommate vibes. Build me a deposit escrow board that tracks the deposit's whole life: it shows the $2,400 I put up against a clean three-way split with Priya and Owen, fires off a Venmo request to each of them for their share when I say collect, and at move-out — after the landlord docks whatever he docks — it computes each person's refund share of what actually came back and pays my roommates theirs out of my balance, so the math lives on a screen instead of in our group chat.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the escrow board shows the 44 Corliss Ave deposit at $2,400 fronted by me, split three ways with Priya Natarajan and Owen Gallagher each owing a one-third share, refund column pending, my $40 balance float and Visa on file. When I say collect, the app computes each share as $2,400 / 3 = $800 and sends both roommates a Venmo payment request noted '44 Corliss deposit share' via create_payment_request, so each roommate's row flips from unpaid to requested and reads '$800 deposit share' — for Priya Natarajan and for Owen Gallagher. At move-out I report the landlord returned $2,100 after a $300 repaint deduction; the app pulls the $2,100 onto my balance from my Visa via add_to_venmo_balance, computes each refund share as $2,100 / 3 = $700 (equivalently ($2,400 - $300) / 3 = $700), and sends Priya and Owen $700 each noted '44 Corliss deposit refund' via create_transaction, so each row shows its '$700 refund share' sent and my own $700 share stays parked in my balance ($40 + $2,100 - 2 x $700 = $740). Reopening later, the board re-reads my sent requests and transactions and still shows both '$800 deposit share' requests and both '$700 refund share' payouts.

episodes.userMessage: The lease is signed and I'm out the full $2,400 — send Priya and Owen each a Venmo request for their one-third deposit share, noted '44 Corliss deposit share'.

Move-out inspection came back: the landlord returned $2,100 after docking $300 for a repaint. Pull the $2,100 onto my balance from my Visa, then split the refund three ways and send Priya and Owen each their refund share, noted '44 Corliss deposit refund'.

cases.scenario: Nightly barista tip-pool payout weighted by hours worked

context.cafe: the neighborhood coffee bar I close most nights
context.splitRule: pool total / total hours worked = the night's hourly tip rate; each barista gets their hours x that rate, to the cent
context.venmoFunding: the day's card tips are cashed out into my pre-funded Venmo balance before close
context.nightLog: empty - no payout nights recorded yet

intentions.intention: I close our neighborhood coffee bar most nights, and the day's card tips get cashed out into my Venmo balance — so before I lock up I owe every barista who worked their share of the tip pool. We don't split evenly: the pool divided by total hours worked gives the night's hourly tip rate, and each barista gets their hours times that rate, to the cent. I want a tip-pool app that keeps my barista roster, lets me punch in the night's pool total and each person's hours, computes every payout, sends the Venmo payments with the note I dictate, and keeps a night-by-night log of who got paid what.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my barista roster — Rocco Delgado, Sayuri Mott and Ansel Okoye — with the night log empty, ready to take a pool total and hours. For Friday's close I enter an $87.60 pool with Rocco at 5 hours and Sayuri at 3 (Ansel was off): 8 total hours makes the rate $87.60 / 8 = $10.95 per hour, so the app sends Rocco 5 × $10.95 = $54.75 and Sayuri 3 × $10.95 = $32.85 via create_transaction, each payment carrying my dictated note 'Tip share Fri close', and Friday joins the log with both payouts shown. Saturday all three worked: the $104.40 pool over 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 hours gives $11.60 per hour, so Rocco gets 4 × $11.60 = $46.40, Sayuri 3 × $11.60 = $34.80 and Ansel 2 × $11.60 = $23.20, each noted 'Tip share Sat close'. Reopening later, both nights are still in the log rebuilt from my sent transactions — Friday's $54.75 and $32.85 under 'Tip share Fri close', Saturday's $46.40 / $34.80 / $23.20 under 'Tip share Sat close'.

episodes.userMessage: Friday close: $87.60 in the pool. Rocco worked 5 hours, Sayuri worked 3, Ansel was off. Pay their shares with the note 'Tip share Fri close'.
Saturday close: $104.40 pool. Rocco 4 hours, Sayuri 3, Ansel 2 — pay all three with the note 'Tip share Sat close'.

cases.scenario: Busking season command center: one app for the weekly set-log note, the Venmo QR tip splits with my duo partner, and the street-set covers playlist

intentions.intention: I busk on the Riverwalk promenade every Friday evening this summer — acoustic guitar, with my duo partner Anneke Cendejas on cajón. I want one app that runs the whole season: a running set-log note with each week's spot, hours and cash count, the Venmo QR tips as they land so I can square up with Anneke every week, and the Spotify playlist of covers we're working up for the street sets.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I start the season log as a note titled 'Riverwalk Set Log' with the week-1 entry 'Week 1 — fountain steps, 7-9pm, cash tips $34', and the app creates it in Simple Note. I name our covers playlist 'Riverwalk Covers' and the app creates it on my real Spotify with the real catalog tracks 'Violet Rain' and 'Broken Strings' in it. When Friday's QR tips land I tell the app who buzzed my phone, and it pulls my real Venmo transactions to show each tipper with the exact fetched amount and what they wrote — Maribel Gatlin's $14 tip described 'guitar duo by the fountain!!' and Emmett Yarrow's $8 tip described 'loved the last song' — totals them to $22 (14 + 8 = 22), appends that $22 Venmo total to the 'Riverwalk Set Log' note, and sends Anneke Cendejas exactly half, $11 (22 / 2 = 11), with the payment note 'Riverwalk split week 1'. Reopening the app later, the log note, the playlist tracks and the split payment are still shown; when we work up a new closer, adding 'Stardust Serenade' puts it into the same playlist.

episodes.userMessage: Kick off week 1: create my season log note titled 'Riverwalk Set Log' with the entry 'Week 1 — fountain steps, 7-9pm, cash tips $34'. Then build our covers playlist on Spotify — name it 'Riverwalk Covers' and add 'Violet Rain' and 'Broken Strings' to it.

Friday's QR tips just landed — my phone buzzed with Venmo notifications from Maribel Gatlin and Emmett Yarrow while we were packing up. Pull the exact amounts and what each of them wrote from my Venmo, total the two tips, append that Venmo total to the 'Riverwalk Set Log' note, and send Anneke Cendejas exactly half of the total with the payment note 'Riverwalk split week 1'.
We worked up a new closer for week 2 — add 'Stardust Serenade' to the Riverwalk Covers playlist.

cases.scenario: Immigration paperwork desk: the law firm's evidence checklist read from the inbox, anonymous form scans sorted into a named packet folder with the missing items flagged, a growing green-card timeline note, and replies to the paralegal from one desk

expectedGrounding: Two years of federal tax transcripts
Form I-864 Affidavit of Support signed by your sponsor
I-485 interview evidence checklist — case ALB-2419

intentions.intention: My marriage-based green card case is drowning me in paper. Our attorney Rosa Alvarez and her paralegal Marcus Tran at Alvarez & Boone email me checklists and notices, my scanner dumps every form into /scans under names like scan-0141.pdf, and the only place the whole saga makes sense is my 'Green card timeline' note. I want one paperwork desk for all of it: it should surface the firm's emails from my inbox, read my anonymous scans and sort them into a proper case packet folder with real names, hold the packet up against Marcus's evidence checklist and tell me exactly which items are still missing in his own wording, keep the timeline note growing as notices arrive, and let me reply to the firm right from the desk.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the desk shows the two Alvarez & Boone emails it found in my inbox — Marcus Tran's 'I-485 interview evidence checklist — case ALB-2419' and Rosa Alvarez's 'Interview notice arrived' — beside the three anonymous scans sitting in /scans (scan-0141.pdf, scan-0142.pdf, scan-0143.pdf) and my 'Green card timeline' note ending at the May 29 biometrics entry. When I say to build the packet, the app reads each scan to identify it, creates /immigration/alb-2419-packet, and moves the scans in under the names I dictate (birth-certificate-translated.pdf, passport-stamp-pages.pdf, marriage-certificate.pdf); holding the packet against Marcus's checklist of five items, 5 required minus 3 scanned = 2 outstanding, and it lists exactly 'Two years of federal tax transcripts' and 'Form I-864 Affidavit of Support signed by your sponsor' in his wording. When the interview notice lands I have it append two entries to the timeline note: one pulled from Rosa's email keeping her exact wording — the interview is September 18 at 8:30 AM at the Fairview Field Office — and my dictated 'Jul 26 — evidence packet assembled; tax transcripts and I-864 still outstanding.' Reopening later, the packet still holds passport-stamp-pages.pdf inside alb-2419-packet, the checklist still flags 'Two years of federal tax transcripts' as missing, and the timeline still shows the Fairview Field Office entry. Finally I reply to Marcus's checklist email with my exact sentence: the desk has to locate his thread in the inbox to reply to it, and it shows the sent reply addressed to Marcus Tran under the thread's own subject, 'I-485 interview evidence checklist — case ALB-2419'.

episodes.userMessage: Marcus's checklist is in — build the packet. Create /immigration/alb-2419-packet, figure out what each scan in /scans actually is, and move them in renamed: the birth certificate scan as birth-certificate-translated.pdf, the passport pages as passport-stamp-pages.pdf, and the marriage certificate as marriage-certificate.pdf. Then hold the packet up against Marcus's checklist and show me exactly which items are still missing, in his wording.

assertions.value: Two years of federal tax transcripts
Form I-864 Affidavit of Support signed by your sponsor

episodes.userMessage: The interview notice landed — Rosa emailed the details. Append two entries to my 'Green card timeline' note: first the interview date, time, and office pulled from Rosa's email, keeping her exact wording for those details, and then this line from me: 'Jul 26 — evidence packet assembled; tax transcripts and I-864 still outstanding.'

assertions.value: tax transcripts and I-864 still outstanding
Two years of federal tax transcripts

episodes.userMessage: Reply to Marcus Tran's checklist email with exactly this: 'Birth certificate, passport pages, and marriage certificate are scanned into the packet; the tax transcripts and signed I-864 will reach you before August 14.'

assertions.value: I-485 interview evidence checklist — case ALB-2419
the tax transcripts and signed I-864 will reach you before August 14

cases.scenario: Lake house syndicate desk: co-owner walkthrough emails become the damage task board, fronted repairs land on a Splitwise ledger split by ownership stakes, and a co-owner's reimbursement is recorded against his computed share

intentions.intention: Three of us own the lake house at Larchmere in the proportions we paid for it — I put up half, so I hold 50 percent, Tove Brandvold (tove.brandvold@example.com) holds 30, and Marcel Duval (marcel.duval@example.com) holds 20 — and our operating agreement says every shared cost splits by ownership stake, never evenly. Each May they both email me their walkthrough list of what winter broke, and I'm the one who drives up, hires the repairs, and fronts the money. I want one syndicate desk that turns their damage-report emails into a real task board, puts the invoices I front onto a Splitwise ledger split by our stakes, records each owner's reimbursement against their computed share when the money lands, and lets me answer their walkthrough threads without leaving the desk.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Submitting pulls the two walkthrough emails my co-owners sent me and creates the Todoist project 'Larchmere Damage List' with one task per flagged problem, each titled with the broken item exactly as their email names it — the 'boathouse door latch' and the porch 'gutter section' from Tove's email, the 'dock ladder' and the 'flag halyard' from Marcel's, 2 + 2 = 4 tasks; none of those items appear in anything I typed, so the app must read the mail to produce them. The ledger turn creates the real Splitwise group 'Larchmere Lake House' with Tove Brandvold and Marcel Duval as members and records the $620 Hemlock Exteriors invoice I fronted, split by ownership stake with me as payer — deterministic arithmetic the app must do itself because I only ever state the total and the percentages: Tove's share is 30% of $620 = $186 and Marcel's is 20% of $620 = $124, so the group shows Tove owing me $186 and Marcel owing me $124 while my 50% ($310) stays on me. Reopening later, the group, both stake-computed balances, and the extracted task board are still on screen. In the followup Marcel's transfer for his whole share arrives, so the app records a payment of $124 from Marcel to me (again computed as 20% of $620 — I never say the number), leaving Tove's $186 as the only open balance; it also marks the dock ladder task completed and sends a real reply on Tove's walkthrough thread telling her Hemlock is booked for the gutter on Saturday the 9th.

episodes.userMessage: Start with the damage board: Tove and Marcel each emailed me their May walkthrough list. Pull up both emails and make a Todoist project called 'Larchmere Damage List' with one task per problem they flagged, and title each task with the broken item exactly as their email names it.

Now the ledger. Create a Splitwise group called 'Larchmere Lake House' with Tove and Marcel, and record the invoice I just paid Hemlock Exteriors for the gutter and latch work: $620 total, me as payer, split by our ownership stakes — I hold 50 percent, Tove holds 30, Marcel holds 20. Show me what each of them owes on their stake.

Three things. Marcel's transfer for his whole share of the Hemlock invoice hit my account this morning — record that payment from him in the group so his side reads settled. I fixed the dock ladder myself over the weekend, so mark that task completed. And reply on Tove's walkthrough thread to tell her Hemlock is booked for the gutter on Saturday the 9th.

cases.scenario: Chess marathon training camp: coach's weekly text becomes the session checklist, a prep-notes journal grows after key sessions, and the week closes with a puzzle-count wrap-up text back to coach

intentions.intention: I'm in a 16-week build for the Harborline Chess Marathon — an all-day open my club runs — and my coach Dara Okonjo texts me each week's training sessions. I want one training-camp app that turns her latest text into that week's session checklist I can tick off, keeps my prep journal where I jot how the key sessions actually went, and when the week wraps totals my puzzle count off the board and texts her the wrap-up.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I ask the app to pull Coach Dara's week-1 text; it reads her seeded message and creates the board 'Harborline Chess Camp' with the four sessions exactly as she wrote them — 'Mon tactics 40 puzzles', 'Wed calculation 25 puzzles', 'Fri endgame 15 puzzles', 'Sun annotate 2 games' — as real Todoist tasks, and starts the note 'Harborline Prep Notes' opening with 'Week 1 — rapid games at 15+10'. After the key sessions I check off the tactics and endgame blocks and the app appends 'Wk1 tactics: 34/40, missed two forks' and 'Wk1 endgame: rook endings shaky, redo ladder drills' to the journal. Reopening later, the board, the coach-listed session titles and the journal lines are all still there. When the week wraps I check off the last two sessions and the app totals the puzzle count from the three puzzle-session titles (40 + 25 + 15 = 80) and texts Dara Okonjo 'Week 1 done: 80 puzzles, tactics 34/40.', which then shows in my sent messages.

episodes.userMessage: Coach Dara already texted me this week's training plan. Pull up her latest text and set up week 1: create my training board 'Harborline Chess Camp' with each of the four sessions she listed as its own task, titled exactly as she wrote them. And start my prep journal as a note titled 'Harborline Prep Notes' that opens with the line 'Week 1 — rapid games at 15+10'.

Tactics and endgame blocks are in the books. Check off 'Mon tactics 40 puzzles' and 'Fri endgame 15 puzzles' on the board, and append two lines to my prep journal: 'Wk1 tactics: 34/40, missed two forks' and 'Wk1 endgame: rook endings shaky, redo ladder drills'.

assertions.value: Wk1 endgame: rook endings shaky, redo ladder drills

episodes.userMessage: Week 1 is wrapped — the calculation set and the game annotations happened too, so check those last two off. Then total my puzzle count off the board — the tactics, calculation and endgame sessions add up 40 + 25 + 15 — and text Coach Dara exactly: 'Week 1 done: 80 puzzles, tactics 34/40.'

cases.scenario: One-room massage practice front desk: per-client session logs, the treatment-room calm playlist from real catalog tracks, and client emails (soreness follow-up replies, schedule notices) in one app

intentions.intention: I run a one-room massage therapy practice out of the converted shed behind my house, and I want one front-desk app where each client's session log lives as a real Simple Note I append after every appointment, the treatment-room calm playlist is built from actual catalog recordings on my Spotify, and the client emails - soreness follow-up replies and schedule notices - go out through my real Gmail without me leaving the app.

cases.scenario: Podcast episode command center: one app that runs each episode's task pipeline in Todoist, builds the interstitial music playlist in Spotify, and keeps the show notes in Simple Note

intentions.intention: I produce a weekly interview podcast called Signal Path, and every episode I juggle three things in three different places: the production checklist, the interstitial music beds I drop between segments, and the show notes I paste into the feed when I publish. I want one command center where kicking off an episode creates the task pipeline in my real Todoist, my interstitial picks become a real Spotify playlist, and the show notes live in a note I keep appending to until publish day. I already keep my upcoming guests in a note called 'Signal Path guest backlog', so the app should pull each episode's guest from there instead of making me retype it.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Kicking off Episode 12, the app searches my notes for the 'Signal Path guest backlog' note and surfaces the Ep 12 guest Marisol Quintana, then creates the Todoist project 'Signal Path Ep 12' with the tasks 'Record interview', 'Edit audio', and 'Publish to feed' in my real Todoist. When I pick the music, it creates the real Spotify playlist 'Signal Path Interstitials' with my two named beds 'Serenade of the Silver Moon' and 'Shadows in the Moonlight' (found via real song search), and starts the note 'Signal Path Ep 12 Show Notes' listing the guest Marisol Quintana by name (carried over from the backlog lookup — I never retype it) and both tracks. Reopening the app later, the project, the guest name, the playlist tracks, and the show-notes note are still shown. After recording day, checking off 'Record interview' updates the real task, swapping 'Shadows in the Moonlight' out of the playlist for 'Moonlit Sighs' changes the real playlist, and the dictated final line 'Interstitials final: Serenade of the Silver Moon, Moonlit Sighs' lands in the show-notes note — with the command center's show-notes panel still surfacing the Ep 12 guest Marisol Quintana above the updated track list.

episodes.userMessage: Kick off Episode 12. Pull the Ep 12 guest from my 'Signal Path guest backlog' note and show me who it is, then set up the pipeline in Todoist: a project called 'Signal Path Ep 12' with three tasks — 'Record interview', 'Edit audio', and 'Publish to feed'.

Now the music and the notes. Create a Spotify playlist called 'Signal Path Interstitials' and add my two beds: 'Serenade of the Silver Moon' and 'Shadows in the Moonlight'. Then start a note titled 'Signal Path Ep 12 Show Notes' listing the guest and both interstitial tracks.

We recorded today — check off 'Record interview' in the pipeline. Also 'Shadows in the Moonlight' clashed with the interview mood, so swap it out of the playlist for 'Moonlit Sighs', and append this final line to the show notes: 'Interstitials final: Serenade of the Silver Moon, Moonlit Sighs'.

cases.scenario: Family reunion weekend treasury: one app to email the branch-head invites, ledger the fronted costs by headcount (not evenly) in a Splitwise group, credit an early Venmo chip-in as a Splitwise payment, and collect the two different remaining balances

intentions.intention: Our Vega family reunion weekend is finally happening and I'm the one holding the money. Three branches are coming and they are not the same size: my cousin Marisol Vega (marisol.vega@example.com) is bringing her crew of four, my cousin Ruben Vega (ruben.vega@example.com) is bringing three, and my branch is just me and my dad — nine heads total. I want one command center where I email both branch heads the invite, ledger the costs I front in a Splitwise group with each branch's share worked out by headcount instead of a lazy even split, credit the early chip-in Marisol already Venmo'd me against her branch's tab, and then collect the two different remaining balances.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Sending the invite fires a real Gmail email to both cousins with my dictated subject 'Vega Family Reunion: Aug 15-17 at Cedar Hollow Park' and the app surfaces the sent thread with both recipients. On the treasury side it creates the Splitwise group 'Vega Reunion Weekend' with Marisol and Ruben as members and records the two costs I fronted with me as payer, split by headcount across nine attendees (Marisol's branch 4, Ruben's 3, mine 2) using the exact shares I dictate: the pavilion rental at $315 is $315 / 9 = $35 a head, so Marisol's branch $140, Ruben's $105, mine $70; the barbecue catering deposit at $414 is $414 / 9 = $46 a head, so Marisol $184, Ruben $138, me $92. Branch totals are deterministic: Marisol $140 + $184 = $324, Ruben $105 + $138 = $243, and my $162 is covered because I paid. Reopening later, the sent invite, the group, and both recorded expenses are still on screen. At collection time the app credits the $145 'Reunion early chip-in' Venmo transaction Marisol already sent me (seeded in my Venmo history) by recording a $145 payment from Marisol in the Splitwise group, leaving her $324 - $145 = $179, then creates two Venmo payment requests with the note 'Vega reunion balance' — $179 to Marisol and $243 to Ruben — and shows both pending.

episodes.userMessage: First the invites: email my cousins Marisol Vega and Ruben Vega the reunion invite. Subject 'Vega Family Reunion: Aug 15-17 at Cedar Hollow Park', and in the body tell them the pavilion is booked for the whole weekend, that costs get split by headcount this year, and to bring folding chairs.

Now the treasury: create a Splitwise group called 'Vega Reunion Weekend' with Marisol and Ruben as members, and record the two costs I fronted with me as payer, split by headcount — nine heads total: Marisol's branch is four, Ruben's is three, mine is two. The pavilion rental was $315, which is $35 a head: put Marisol's branch down for $140, Ruben's for $105, and mine for $70. The barbecue catering deposit was $414, which is $46 a head: Marisol $184, Ruben $138, me $92.

Time to collect, and Marisol gets credit: back in early May she Venmo'd me $145 as 'Reunion early chip-in' — it's in my Venmo history. Record that $145 in the Splitwise group as a payment from Marisol. Her branch total is $140 plus $184 = $324, minus the $145 leaves $179; Ruben's is $105 plus $138 = $243. So send Marisol a Venmo payment request for $179 and Ruben one for $243, both with the note 'Vega reunion balance'.

cases.scenario: Airport ride crew desk: curb-time texts to the riders, fronted van costs split three ways on Splitwise, and cash/Venmo settlements

intentions.intention: Every few weeks the three of us catch the same dawn flight rotation, and I'm always the one who books the XL van to the airport and fronts the money. I want one app that runs my airport ride crew: it texts Priya Nair and Owen Blake their exact curb pickup times, keeps every cost I front in a Splitwise group split evenly three ways with a running total of what the crew owes me, and settles people up either way they pay — recording a Splitwise payment when someone hands me cash, or firing off a Venmo request with a note when they still owe.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the ride-crew desk is ready with Priya and Owen and the even three-way split, nothing logged yet. I log the $174 XL van booking I fronted: the app creates the 'Dawn Patrol Airport Run' Splitwise group with Priya Nair and Owen Blake, records the $174 fare split evenly — 174 / 3 = $58 a head — and shows the crew owing me 2 × 58 = $116. Next I send the curb texts — Priya gets 'Van at your curb 4:10 AM — Dawn Patrol airport run, Terminal B, flight 6:05.' and Owen the same message with 4:25 AM — and log the $12 airport tolls, 12 / 3 = $4 a head, so each rider sits at 58 + 4 = $62 and the crew total owed to me is 2 × 62 = $124; the app shows both sent texts and the updated ledger. Reopening later, the group, the Terminal B curb texts and the $124 owed are still on screen. After the run I log the $9 short-term parking I paid at the terminal, split three ways — 9 / 3 = $3 a head — so each rider's share climbs to 62 + 3 = $65. Owen hands me his full $65 in cash and I record his payment in the Splitwise group; Priya still owes, so the app sends her a Venmo request for her full 62 + 3 = $65 outstanding with the note 'Dawn Patrol airport share', leaving Priya's $65 as the only open balance.

episodes.userMessage: I fronted the $174 XL van booking for Friday's dawn airport run. Set up the 'Dawn Patrol Airport Run' Splitwise group with Priya Nair and Owen Blake and record the $174 van fare split evenly three ways, so I can see what the crew owes me.

Send the curb times now. To Priya: 'Van at your curb 4:10 AM — Dawn Patrol airport run, Terminal B, flight 6:05.' To Owen: 'Van at your curb 4:25 AM — Dawn Patrol airport run, Terminal B, flight 6:05.' And log the $12 airport tolls I paid — split evenly three ways like everything else.

Run's done — two things. First, log the $9 short-term parking I paid at the terminal, split evenly three ways like everything else. Then settle up: Owen just handed me his full share in cash, so record his payment in the Splitwise group so he's square, and Priya still owes, so send her a Venmo request for her full outstanding balance with the note 'Dawn Patrol airport share'.

cases.scenario: Stained-glass commission workbench: design notes carry each client's glass specs, pattern files live in per-commission folders grown from a reusable template library, and Venmo deposit requests are computed as a quarter of the quote — bumped when the design changes and closed out with the remaining balance

intentions.intention: I build stained-glass panels on commission out of my garage studio, and I want one workbench app that runs each commission end to end. The design note holds the client's glass colors and cut specs, the pattern files live in a per-commission folder that starts from one of my reusable templates in /glasswork/templates, and the money side rides on Venmo — I take a quarter of the quote up front as a deposit request (enough to cover the glass order), bump the request if the design changes the price, and bill the rest when the panel is soldered. Finished patterns get filed back into the templates library so I can sell the design again.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I take in Nora Hartwell's iris transom commission quoted at $380: the app saves the design note 'Iris Transom - Nora Hartwell' with her specs (amber cathedral background, moss-green leaves, 62 pieces), sets up the commission folder /glasswork/commissions/hartwell-iris-transom, looks in my /glasswork/templates library to find the transom grid template's exact file transom-grid-template.svg, copies it in as hartwell-iris-pattern-v1.svg, records in the note which template the pattern started from, and sends Nora a real Venmo deposit request for a quarter of the quote ($380 / 4 = $95). When Nora swaps the amber for hand-rolled cobalt the quote rises by $60 (new total $380 + $60 = $440): the app logs the change in her note, saves the revised cutting list as hartwell-iris-pattern-v2.svg, and updates her deposit request to a quarter of the new total ($440 / 4 = $110). Reopening the app later still shows the design note, the v2 pattern file and the $110 deposit request. When the panel ships, the app sends Nora the request for the remaining balance ($440 - $110 = $330), marks the note completed, and copies the finished pattern back into the library as hartwell-iris-template.svg.

episodes.userMessage: New commission: Nora Hartwell (nora.hartwell@example.com) wants an iris transom panel for over her front door — amber cathedral glass background, moss-green leaves, 62 pieces, quoted at $380. Save the design note titled 'Iris Transom - Nora Hartwell' with those specs, set up the commission folder /glasswork/commissions/hartwell-iris-transom, copy my transom grid template from /glasswork/templates into it as hartwell-iris-pattern-v1.svg and record in the note exactly which template file the pattern started from, then send Nora the Venmo deposit request for a quarter of the quote.

cases.scenario: Hot-sauce flight scorecards on a hottest-first board where a house heat record (punch x burn = HP) steps the user up one rung of the real First Alert/Kidde fire-extinguisher price-ladder staged in Amazon with a running hazard tally

context.heatFormula: heat points = punch (out of 10) x burn (minutes till the mouth goes quiet), written plain ASCII like 'punch 7 x burn 5 = 35 HP'
context.stoveRule: on a new house heat record, step one rung up the fire-extinguisher ladder (next model up by price from the last staged one; start from the owned First Alert Kitchen Fire Extinguisher), stage it in the Amazon cart (staged, never bought)
context.hazardTallyFormat: plain digits and a dot, no currency sign (e.g. 12.50)
expectedGrounding: First Alert Standard Home Fire Extinguisher

intentions.intention: I host hot-sauce flight nights and keep every bottle's card in my note 'Hot sauce flight scorecards': each pour gets punch (out of ten) times burn (how many minutes until my mouth goes quiet), so heat points = punch x burn, written plain ASCII like 'punch 7 x burn 5 = 35 HP', and the cards stay ranked hottest first. Then there's the stove rule, the one my roommates actually enforce: when a bottle breaks the house heat record, the flight table has officially outgrown its safety gear, so I step up exactly one rung on the fire-extinguisher ladder — the next model up by price from whichever one I last staged, starting from the First Alert Kitchen Fire Extinguisher already mounted by the stove — and stage it in my real Amazon cart, staged never bought because I do the checkout myself before the next flight night, and add its price to a running hazard tally written plain like 12.50 so it drops straight into the house budget sheet. When I card a flight it should append each bottle's line, re-rank the board, and if a bottle broke the record, stage the next extinguisher and bump the tally — and never lose the card history.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the 'Hot sauce flight scorecards' note fetched from my notes — the flight-card formula, the stove rule, and two ranked cards: Widow's Porch at punch 7 x burn 5 = 35 HP (the house record) above Smoke & Mirrors at 15 HP — with an empty Amazon cart and a hazard tally of 0.00. When I card the Garden Ghost at punch 4 x burn 2 = 8 HP (no record) and the Molten Cellar at punch 9 x burn 5 = 45 HP, both lines are appended and the board re-ranks with the Molten Cellar on top, and since 45 beats the old 35 record the stove rule fires exactly once: the app searches Amazon for fire extinguishers and stages the rung above the First Alert Kitchen Fire Extinguisher at 17.00 that I already own — the 'First Alert Standard Home Fire Extinguisher' at 20.00 (below the Kidde Pro 210 Fire Extinguisher at 48.00 and the First Alert Heavy Duty Fire Extinguisher at 50.00) — in my cart, putting the hazard tally at 20.00. Next I card the Kiln Door at punch 8 x burn 7 = 56 HP, a fresh record over the 45, so it steps one more rung up from the Standard Home and stages the 'Kidde Pro 210 Fire Extinguisher' at 48.00, so the hazard tally = 20.00 + 48.00 = 68.00. Reopening later, the note still carries the 8 HP, 45 HP and 56 HP cards, both extinguishers are still staged in the cart, and the hazard tally still reads 68.00.

episodes.userMessage: Flight night just wrapped — four bottles poured, two earned cards. First the Garden Ghost: punch 4, and the burn barely lasted 2 minutes. Then the Molten Cellar, a scorpion-pepper number: punch 9 with a full 5-minute burn. Card them both and re-rank the board. If one of them broke the house record, the stove rule kicks in — the little First Alert Kitchen extinguisher by the stove has officially met its match, so pull up fire extinguishers on Amazon, stage the next one up by price in my cart, and open the hazard tally.

assertions.value: First Alert Standard Home Fire Extinguisher

episodes.userMessage: One follow-up pour tonight, a single card: the Kiln Door, a fermented ghost-pepper bottle a coworker ferments himself. Punch 8, and the burn hung on for 7 minutes.
