intentions.intention: I'm finally filing the non-provisional patent on my self-venting fermentation lid and the paperwork sprawls across three places: my attorney Ingrid Kaufmann at Kestrel & Doyle emails me fee schedules and search-report findings under our docket, the claim drafts live as versioned files in /patent/claims, and every prior-art reference we have to argue around belongs in my 'Prior-art log — fermenting lid' note. I want a filing war room that pulls it all together: surface Ingrid's emails from my inbox, read the live claim file and hold its claim count against her fee schedule so I always see the filing total we'd owe, spin up each new claim-set version as a copy so I never edit the old one directly, log every search-report reference into the prior-art note under her exact citation with my distinguishing argument beneath it, and email her from the room when the set is ready to file.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the war room shows Ingrid Kaufmann's two Kestrel & Doyle emails from my inbox — 'Docket KD-2071 — non-provisional fees and claim count' and 'KD-2071 search report — two references to distinguish' — beside the claim files in /patent/claims (claims-v2.md and the current claims-v3.md) and my 'Prior-art log — fermenting lid' note with its single Kim entry. When I ask for the damage, the app reads claims-v3.md (its header and Ingrid's email both state the set is 23 claims) and her small-entity schedule and computes the total: $130 + $280 + $320 = $730 base, 23 - 20 = 3 excess claims x $50 = $150, $730 + $150 = $880, pinning the fee line in my dictated form as 'Filing total: $880'; it also creates claims-v4.md as a copy of v3 so I have a working file. From the search-report email it appends both references to the prior-art note keeping Ingrid's citations verbatim — US 8,642,077 (Hollenbeck) and US 9,157,304 (Brandt) — each over my dictated distinguishing argument, ending 'ours self-seats after every vent' for Brandt. Reopening later, claims-v4.md still sits in /patent/claims and the note still carries US 8,642,077, US 9,157,304, and the self-seats argument. Finally I trim dependent claims 21, 22, and 23 out of claims-v4.md to sit at 20 claims flat; with the three excess claims gone the fee line falls back to 'Filing total: $730' ($880 - $150 = $730 — the excess-claim charge gone), and the room sends Ingrid Kaufmann my dictated status email under the subject 'KD-2071 claims trimmed to twenty'.

episodes.userMessage: Ingrid's fee email is in — work out the damage. Read the current claim set (claims-v3.md is the latest in /patent/claims) and her small-entity fee schedule, and pin what we'd owe as things stand at the top of the desk as a line reading 'Filing total: $X' with the real number in place of X. Then create claims-v4.md as a copy of v3 so I have a working file and never touch v3 directly.

Ingrid's search report flags two references — get them into my 'Prior-art log — fermenting lid' note. Append both, keeping her citation for each exactly as she wrote it, and under each add my argument: for the Hollenbeck vent write 'distinguished: releases on a fixed factory spring, not a user-set threshold'; for the Brandt valve write 'distinguished: needs hand-priming before every batch; ours self-seats after every vent'.

Time to get under the cap. In claims-v4.md, drop dependent claims 21, 22, and 23 — the sensor-housing dependents — so the set sits at exactly 20 claims, and refresh the 'Filing total: $X' line to what we owe now. Then email Ingrid Kaufmann with subject 'KD-2071 claims trimmed to twenty' and exactly this body: 'Claims v4 drops the three sensor-housing dependents, so we are at 20 claims flat and the excess-claim charge goes away. Green light to file when you are ready.'

cases.scenario: Wedding DJ booking desk: per-couple must-play playlists from the real catalog, confirmation texts to the couple's contact, and 25%-of-package Venmo deposit requests

intentions.intention: I DJ weddings most Saturdays from spring through fall, and every couple I book needs the same three things handled before I pencil them in: their must-play request playlist started in my real Spotify, a confirmation text to whoever handles their planning, and the deposit request sent on Venmo — I always collect 25% of the package price up front. I want one booking desk app where each booked couple is a card with their wedding date, contact person, package, and deposit status, and where running intake for a couple drives all three apps from that one card.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I book the Ferreira-Blake wedding for October 17: the app creates a real playlist in my Spotify named exactly 'Ferreira-Blake 10/17 Must-Plays' and seeds it by searching the catalog for their two dictated must-plays, 'Unfolding the Map of Us' and 'Azure Skies' (both real country tracks), rounding it out with more country from the catalog; the card shows the playlist with those titles. Next turn I finish their intake: the app texts my contact Nadia Ferreira the confirmation 'Locked in for October 17 - deposit request on its way', sends her a Venmo payment request for the deposit — Silver package $1,050 at my 25% rule, so 1050 x 0.25 = $262.50 — and adds her late third must-play 'Desert Mirage' to the playlist; the card shows the sent text, the pending $262.50 request, and the updated tracklist. Reopening the app later, the Ferreira-Blake card still shows the 'Ferreira-Blake 10/17 Must-Plays' playlist with 'Azure Skies', the text to Nadia Ferreira, and the $262.50 deposit request. Then a second couple signs and the app runs the same intake for Raman-Whitfield on November 7: playlist 'Raman-Whitfield 11/7 Must-Plays' started with their pop must-play 'Velvet Skies' from the catalog, the confirmation text 'You're on the calendar for November 7' to Cole Whitfield, and a Venmo deposit request on the Gold package — 1530 x 0.25 = $382.50.

episodes.userMessage: First booking of the season: the Ferreira-Blake wedding, October 17. Start their must-play playlist in my Spotify, named exactly 'Ferreira-Blake 10/17 Must-Plays' — they're a country couple. Their two must-plays are 'Unfolding the Map of Us' and 'Azure Skies'; find those in the catalog, add them, and round the list out with a few more country tracks.

Now finish the Ferreira-Blake intake. Text Nadia Ferreira: 'Locked in for October 17 - deposit request on its way'. Then send her the Venmo payment request for the deposit — they took the Silver package at $1,050 and I always collect 25% up front, so work out the amount and request exactly that. And Nadia just texted a third must-play: add 'Desert Mirage' to their playlist.

Second couple just signed: Raman-Whitfield, November 7, and Cole Whitfield is my contact. Run the same intake — playlist named exactly 'Raman-Whitfield 11/7 Must-Plays' starting with their pop must-play 'Velvet Skies' from the catalog, text Cole 'You're on the calendar for November 7', and send him the Venmo deposit request: Gold package at $1,530, same 25% rule.

cases.scenario: Food-truck weekend prep board swept board-to-note into one service-day runsheet

context.truck: Sunbird taco truck (weekend residency in the Copperhook Brewing taproom lot)
context.sweepDirection: REVERSED sync: the Todoist board is the source; every open prep task becomes one line of a single service-day note
seededPrepTasks: Marinate 25 lb pork shoulder for the al pastor
Dice 15 lb tomatillos for the salsa verde
Batch 3 gallons of hibiscus agua fresca
Press 200 tortillas and stack them in the warmer
Swap both 40 lb propane tanks at the depot
Print 60 menu cards with the weekend special

intentions.intention: I run the Sunbird taco truck, and every weekend we park in the Copperhook Brewing taproom lot. All week prep piles onto my Todoist board 'Sunbird weekend prep' — marinades, salsa batches, propane swaps — but inside the truck nobody thumbs through a task app with wet gloves. I want an app that shows me the board and, at Friday close, sweeps it the reverse direction into one note called 'Copperhook service runsheet', one line per open prep task, that my line cook Rosa reads taped next to the flat-top. Through the weekend I report things once and they land in both places: finished prep gets checked off the board, and anything the commissary springs on us late goes onto the board AND gets appended to the runsheet note, with a running open-task count so I always know how deep the hole is.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my Todoist board 'Sunbird weekend prep' with its six open prep tasks — 'Marinate 25 lb pork shoulder for the al pastor', 'Dice 15 lb tomatillos for the salsa verde', 'Batch 3 gallons of hibiscus agua fresca', 'Press 200 tortillas and stack them in the warmer', 'Swap both 40 lb propane tanks at the depot', 'Print 60 menu cards with the weekend special' — and no runsheet note yet. At Friday close I say sweep, and it creates the note 'Copperhook service runsheet' carrying all 6 open board tasks as 6 note lines, board to note. When Rosa finishes the tortilla pressing I report it once: the app checks 'Press 200 tortillas and stack them in the warmer' off the board (6 − 1 = 5 open), and the commissary's late add that I dictate — 'Thaw 12 lb shrimp for the Sunday ceviche special' — goes onto the board as a new open task (5 + 1 = 6 open of 7 total) and is appended as the runsheet's 7th line. Reopening later, the note 'Copperhook service runsheet' still ends with the shrimp line and the board still holds all seven tasks with the tortilla task completed.

episodes.userMessage: Friday close-down. Sweep the prep board into the runsheet now: make one note called 'Copperhook service runsheet' with one line for every open task on the board.

assertions.value: Marinate 25 lb pork shoulder for the al pastor
Batch 3 gallons of hibiscus agua fresca

episodes.userMessage: Rosa just finished pressing the tortillas — check that one off the board. And the commissary called with a late add: Thaw 12 lb shrimp for the Sunday ceviche special. Put it on the board and append it to the runsheet note.

assertions.value: Thaw 12 lb shrimp for the Sunday ceviche special
Press 200 tortillas and stack them in the warmer

value: Thaw 12 lb shrimp for the Sunday ceviche special

cases.scenario: Shared woodshop bay: machine costs split by logged machine-hours

context.splitRule: each machine bill is split in proportion to the machine-hours each member logged on the hour-meter sheet for that period

intentions.intention: Three of us share Bay 4 at the Grain & Kerf community woodshop — me, Maren Okerlund, and Casimir Quintrell — and the big machines are the whole reason we rent it: the cabinet saw, the planer, the 22-inch drum sander. The bills those machines generate — blade sharpening, fresh abrasive wraps, service visits — land on whoever's turn it is to pay, but splitting them evenly never felt fair because I mill hardwood all weekend while Casimir cuts a few parts a month. So we keep an hour-meter sheet taped to the dust collector: everyone logs their machine-hours, and each bill gets split in proportion to the hours logged for that period. I want an app that keeps a 'Bay 4 Machine Fund' Splitwise group for the three of us, where I enter a bill, who paid it, and that period's meter readings, and it records the expense with each member's share proportional to their logged hours and shows the running balances so nobody has to do long division at the lumber rack.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the Bay 4 machine fund ready to ledger: my baymates Maren Okerlund and Casimir Quintrell named and the hours-proportional split rule spelled out, with no costs logged yet (no splitwise state exists until I create it). I create the 'Bay 4 Machine Fund' group with Maren and Casimir and log the $117 Bearclaw Sharpening invoice I paid, split by the July meter readings — me 14 h, Maren 8 h, Casimir 4 h, so 14 + 8 + 4 = 26 machine-hours and 117 / 26 = $4.50 per machine-hour: my own share is 14 × 4.50 = $63.00, Maren owes 8 × 4.50 = $36.00 and Casimir owes 4 × 4.50 = $18.00. When Casimir covers the $84 Tri-County Abrasives drum-sander order and I enter the August readings — me 8 h, Maren 6 h, Casimir 7 h, so 21 hours and 84 / 21 = $4.00 per machine-hour — the app records the expense with Casimir as payer (my share 8 × 4.00 = $32.00, Maren's 6 × 4.00 = $24.00, his own 7 × 4.00 = $28.00) and the balance view re-renders: Maren owes me $36.00 and owes Casimir $24.00, while my $32.00 share of his bill nets against the $18.00 he owed me from the sharpening invoice, leaving me owing Casimir 32.00 − 18.00 = $14.00. Reopening before the next shop day, the group still shows the Bearclaw Sharpening and Tri-County Abrasives expenses and the standing balances — Maren's $36.00 to me and my net $14.00 to Casimir.

episodes.userMessage: Set up our 'Bay 4 Machine Fund' group with Maren Okerlund and Casimir Quintrell. The July hour-meter sheet reads: me 14 machine-hours, Maren 8, Casimir 4. Log the $117 Bearclaw Sharpening invoice I paid, split in proportion to those hours, and show me what each of them owes.

Casimir covered the $84 Tri-County Abrasives order for the drum sander — new wraps and belts. The August meter sheet reads: me 8 hours, Maren 6, Casimir 7. Log it with him as the payer, split by those hours, and show where everyone's balance lands now.

cases.scenario: Moving-crew bid board: signing deletes the losing bids and opens a running tab at bid minus the flat holding fee, then each cash payment chains off the tab

bidsOnBoard: Two Rivers Transfer - bid $790, cheapest but adds a stair surcharge on site
Sturdy Oak Moving - bid $865, crew of two, no weekend slots
Petrelli Bros Moving - bid $915, three-man crew and they'll take the upright piano
Beacon Hill Haulers - bid $980, only if we move on a Tuesday
context.feeMechanic: movers lock the date with a flat holding fee (a fixed dollar amount, never a percentage); the fee and any cash handed to the crew later come straight off the bill
context.runningTab: single task 'Owed to <company>: $<amount>' whose dollar figure drops with every payment; losing bids get deleted at signing, the winning bid line survives untouched

intentions.intention: The keys to the Mulberry Street place are mine August 1, and four moving crews have walked my apartment and left bids - I keep each one as a task in my 'Mulberry Street Move - Bids In' project, the dollar figure plus whatever caveat came with it. Movers around here lock in your date with a flat holding fee, a fixed dollar amount that comes straight off the bill, and any cash I hand the crew later comes off too. The day I sign with one, I want the app to delete the three losing bids from the board - but leave the winning bid line exactly where it is, since that's my record of what they promised - and open a running tab as a single task, 'Owed to <company>: $<amount>', starting at their bid minus the holding fee I paid. From then on, every time I tell it I handed the crew money, it subtracts that payment from the tab task itself, so the dollar figure always shows what's actually left on the bill.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my seeded 'Mulberry Street Move - Bids In' project with four bid tasks: 'Two Rivers Transfer - bid $790, cheapest but adds a stair surcharge on site', 'Sturdy Oak Moving - bid $865, crew of two, no weekend slots', 'Petrelli Bros Moving - bid $915, three-man crew and they'll take the upright piano', and 'Beacon Hill Haulers - bid $980, only if we move on a Tuesday'. I sign with Petrelli Bros - not the low bid, but the only crew that will take the piano - and pay their flat $180 holding fee, so the app deletes the Two Rivers Transfer, Sturdy Oak Moving and Beacon Hill Haulers bid tasks, leaves the Petrelli bid line untouched, reads the $915 off that line, and opens the tab task 'Owed to Petrelli Bros: $735' because 915 - 180 = 735. On prep day I hand crew lead Nino $250 in cash toward the bill, and the app takes the tab it computed last turn and subtracts again: 735 - 250 = 485, updating the task to read 'Owed to Petrelli Bros: $485'. Reopening later, the board still shows the untouched 'Petrelli Bros Moving - bid $915, three-man crew and they'll take the upright piano' line and the tab still reads 'Owed to Petrelli Bros: $485'.

episodes.userMessage: I signed with Petrelli Bros Moving at the kitchen table this morning - they're the only crew that'll take the upright piano - and handed them their flat $180 holding fee, which comes straight off the bill. Delete the three losing bids from the board, leave the Petrelli line alone, and open my running tab: one task that reads 'Owed to Petrelli Bros: $' followed by what's actually left after the fee.
Nino from the Petrelli crew dropped off the wardrobe boxes this afternoon and I handed him $250 in cash toward the bill. Take that off the running tab so the task shows what's left.

value: Petrelli Bros Moving - bid $915, three-man crew and they'll take the upright piano
